summary: Steel tower recorded at Mackey, Ontario, at 415 m (1362 ft) and placed on a 1963 Department of Lands and Forests map; no build date or current status found.

facts.agency: Ontario Department of Lands and Forests

events.note: Appears on the Department of Lands and Forests Tower Detection System Map (1963), per Firelookout.ca. A map entry, not a build or removal date.

evidence.supports: Tower appears on the 1963 Department of Lands and Forests Tower Detection System Map
evidence.quote: Appears on the Department of Lands and Forests Tower Detection System Map (1963).

evidence.supports: Most Ontario towers erected 1920s-1950s; the period is described as the heyday of forest fire protection
evidence.quote: Most of the towers were erected between the 1920's and the 1950's when forest fire protection was in it's heyday.

evidence.supports: Towers came under the former Department of Lands and Forests, which became the Ministry of Natural Resources in 1972
evidence.quote: They came under the jurisdiction of Ontario's former Department of Lands and Forests which became the Ministry of Natural Resources in 1972.

evidence.supports: Towers were placed to get the best possible view between each tower
evidence.quote: Towers were arranged over the years in specific spots to get the best view possible between each tower.

evidence.supports: Planners usually chose a naturally high elevation for a tower
evidence.quote: Usually the best bet was to put an early warning tower on top of a naturally high elevation like a sloping hill.

sources.title: Ontario's Fire Tower Lookouts: Preserving Their History

notes_for_editor: Only one source names this tower: the Firelookout.ca record, which gives the location as Mackey, Ontario, Canada, a steel tower type, the site elevation, and the 1963 map entry. The record gives no build date, tower height, status or staffing. The Fitzgerald tower is not on either copy of the 'Ontario Fire Towers Still Standing' list (geocities and forestrangers), but that list is undated, its author says it is being kept as it is, and it may be incomplete, so current status is unknown. Two searches and the page reads found no other page about this tower. The 1920s-1950s, Department of Lands and Forests and towermen context comes from the Ontario site's general pages, not this tower's record, and the story says so only by its placement. The 1963 map on the forestrangers site (map1963.jpg, described as showing tower locations and forest districts) was not read and may show this tower; it was not checked. The agency fact rests on the 1963 map title and the general Ontario jurisdiction statement. Confidence is low because the story rests on one register entry plus general context.
